Answer: B
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows dense consolidation in the right upper lobe with a characteristic bulging minor fissure, suggestive of Klebsiella pneumonia. The follow-up image (Figure 3) demonstrates progression to cavitation and necrotizing changes within the same region, while the final image (Figure 5c) shows residual fibrosis/scarring, matching the description in option B.
